title: Border and Cipher Revisited
premise: Orsen Winterbourne, a freelance interpreter who quietly resolves the cases peace delegations prefer to bury, is summoned to translate for a summit everyone privately expects to collapse. When a dead delegate's voiceprint unlocks an encrypted server in another hemisphere, Orsen discovers a sabotage plot engineered to look like an industrial accident — one that will kill the treaty, the truth, and thousands of bystanders. Pursued by both the conspirators and the intelligence service that once employed them, Orsen must decide whether loyalty to their old handler or the truth serves justice. In the end, Orsen broadcasts the evidence at the cost of their own anonymity, exposing the conspiracy and inheriting — at last — a name and a life that are genuinely their own.
about_author: Ada Brightwater is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where nothing said was ever quite what was meant. They write thrillers about people whose professions demand invisibility.

chapters.title: The Language of Failure
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Arriving at the summit city, Orsen interprets a preliminary session already poisoned by bad faith, quietly brokering a face-saving compromise no one wants on record. Their old handler, Vess, watches from the gallery. The beat is weary competence masking dread: Orsen knows this delegation is designed to fail, and knows they were hired to make the failure look accidental.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. A delegate found dead in his hotel room leaves behind a recorder looping a phrase in a dialect Orsen alone recognizes. Played aloud, it authenticates against a server ping in another continent. Emotional beat: cold fascination curdling into fear as Orsen realizes the dead man chose them deliberately — an inheritance of secrets from a stranger.

chapters.title: What the Server Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen, with interludes from Vess. The unlocked files reveal 'Meridian': a staged infrastructure attack timed to coincide with the summit's collapse, blamed on a scapegoated state. Vess, meanwhile, reports Orsen's curiosity upward. Beat: vertigo — the accident isn't coming; it's scheduled, and Orsen's own contract may be part of the choreography.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: POV: Vess. Vess confronts Orsen privately, offering protection in exchange for silence, invoking debts from Orsen's shadowed past. Flashback fragments reveal how Vess once saved them. Beat: the ache of divided loyalty — Vess believes she's protecting Orsen; Orsen sees the leash being refastened.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Room
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Trapped interpreting a plenary session while Meridian operatives move through the building, Orsen smuggles warnings into their translations — double meanings only two delegates catch. One ally, Minister Adeyemi, signals back. Beat: exhilaration and terror; language becomes both weapon and hiding place.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: Adeyemi. The minister reveals her own stake: her country is the designated scapegoat. She offers Orsen asylum and resources if the evidence surfaces under her flag — but using it means the truth becomes a national instrument, not a universal one. Beat: temptation; justice outside the law still demands a price and an owner.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Meridian identifies Orsen. An 'accidental' gas leak forces evacuation of their hotel; Orsen escapes with the copied server key but loses their cover identity, papers, and safe contacts. Vess warns them to run abroad. Beat: stripped bare — everything Orsen built to stay invisible burns, forcing the choice between flight and fight.

chapters.title: Countdown at the Relay
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen and Vess alternating. Orsen traces the attack trigger to a relay station disguised as a weather facility. Racing there, they find Vess waiting — ordered to stop them, hesitating. Beat: confrontation of loyalties; Vess must choose between the institution that owns her and the person she once pulled out of the fire.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Climax. With minutes before Meridian's window closes, Orsen hijacks the relay to transmit the decrypted evidence globally, while Vess holds off the strike team — fatally wounded buying time. Orsen speaks the dead delegate's phrase aloud as authentication, claiming the inheritance fully. Beat: sacrifice, clarity, and grief fused into resolve.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen, weeks later. The attack is prevented, the treaty salvaged in amended form, and investigations bloom — but Orsen, now publicly named, can never work in the shadows again. Meeting Adeyemi, they decline protection and choose testimony instead. Final beat: quiet resolution — justice outside the law ends when someone steps into the light to own what was done.
